refuted.item: Draft item 1: 'coherent fold axes 20-35 mm long along y', and draft item 3: hairpin zones 'handled by the fold skeleton: a segment entering a fold line's 3 mm neighbourhood ...' (the level-3 skeleton used as the fold frame for X1).
refuted.why: UMB-PHERC0268-RESULT §2-3 and logs/umb/PHerc0268/defects.json: 14,176 defects (median 120 per section) but only 1,656 lines, 90 persisting >= 10 sections (>= 11 mm), 20 passing the stability bar, longest 32-35 mm; of the 215 valid lines all but five are 10-17 mm long. So in any section the large majority of folds (the short-lived +-1/2 dipoles = local kinks and terminating bundles) have NO skeleton line, and the draft's hairpin rule never fires for them; they are handled by the generic link rules, where an oblique fold (mean step up to 1.25 mm per 1.1 mm slab at level 3; 0.97 mm on the longest line) shifts every lamina at fixed x by slope x shift per section, and a gated nearest-ridge link with constant-velocity prediction hops exactly one lamina with perfect template correlation when that shift is near one spacing. Using only the 20 stable lines is a global prior that averages away 1,600+ folds. Also the skeleton was localised at R = 3 mm with max steps of 2.5 mm, i.e. at the size of the '3 mm neighbourhood' itself.
refuted.required_edit: Item 1: replace '20-35 mm' with 'fold lines persist 11-35 mm along y (90 lines >= 11 mm, 20 stable, longest 32-35 mm); most folds are short-lived dipoles present in every section (120 per section)'. Item 3: the fold frame for X1 is a per-section level-2 director-defect map (topo_defects on the level-2 in-section tensor, R = 1.5 and 3 mm, every +-1/2 with sign, tracked section-to-section as part of the X1 event table, cost = one 2-D pass per section); the hairpin rule, the no-bridge rule and the domain exclusions key on this map; the level-3 skeleton is a cross-check only. Neighbourhood radius = max(3 mm, local seam-to-seam packet thickness). Inside any defect neighbourhood the link prediction uses the defect's own tracked displacement, not the segment's.

refuted.item: Draft item 1: 'sheet 100-200 um = 1.5-3 voxels [L3] ... level 2 (34.56 um; sheet 3-6 voxels)'; draft item 3: 'per-branch height maps z_k' called a 'sheet identity field'; domain 'spacing >= 7 vox with a visible gap'.
refuted.why: 100-200 um is the phantom's number (audit_spec U7 '1.4-2.9-voxel sheets', W1 '1.5-vox'), not a PHerc0268 measurement; the only in-file thickness measurement for 0268 is ~35 um per half-layer from one probed m7 chunk (audit_spec X3), i.e. ~70 um per sheet = 2 vox at level 2, at the lower edge of the 2-8 vox ridge band and the '< 2 = debris' cut. audit_spec X0 marks the pitch unsupported. In a crushed stack the layers are in contact over most of the area (gaps 'mostly < 70 um or ash-filled', audit_spec §0), so pitch ~ thickness < 7 vox and the only visible gaps are the seams every 1-4 mm: what level 2 separates between gaps is a packet of ~5-40 sheets. The fixed 7-vox domain threshold is the nested-roll pitch assumption (9-17 vox) in disguise and would leave the tracker tracing seam faces while calling them sheets.
refuted.required_edit: Item 1: 'sheet thickness for 0268 is unmeasured; the one probe gives ~70 um (m7 half-layers ~35 um); phantoms use 100-200 um; the census decides'. Working scale becomes a census OUTPUT: level 2 only if the census p10 single-sheet width >= 3 vox at level 2 AND the separable fraction >= 0.3 (prov.) per region class; otherwise the pilot runs on level-1 crops and a full level-1 pass is recorded as infeasible (8x the level-2 bytes), not assumed. Item 3: rename outputs 'lamina height maps' with a per-lamina class SHEET / PAIR / FUSED (see next item); replace 'spacing >= 7 vox' with the census separability criterion (two peaks with a >= 1-voxel dip, spacing >= census p10 separable pitch), marked (prov.).

refuted.item: Draft item 3: 'width 2-8 vox; > 8 FUSED; < 2 debris' together with 'contact kept as two ids'.
refuted.why: Two sheets pressed together without a resolvable gap (the normal state of a crushed stack) give one bright run of 4-12 vox at level 2 (or ~4 vox if sheets are ~70 um): classified as ONE sheet of width <= 8 vox. The 'contact kept as two ids' clause only fires when the gap is visible, and the 'thickness change > 50 %' break never fires while the contact persists along y, so two sheets are silently fused into one id for the whole run, and X4 then grows one surface over two windings. The converse also holds: a sheet delaminated between its two half-layers (two runs of ~1.5-3 vox with a dip) is counted as two sheets or discarded as debris.
refuted.required_edit: Width classes relative to the census median single-sheet width w_s per 256^2 tile: SHEET <= 1.4 w_s with a visible gap both sides; PAIR 1.4-2.5 w_s; FUSED > 2.5 w_s; HALF: two runs each <= 0.6 w_s separated by <= 1 vox. PAIR/FUSED ids carry no sheet claim, are never grown by X4, and are handed to X2 (count) and X3 (R|V grammar); HALF pairs are merged only by X3's cleavage rule with thickness sum <= 1.2 w_s. Every id carries its width class in the event table and the status vocabulary.

refuted.item: Draft item 3: 'bridging over unobserved gaps <= 2 mm only when both neighbours link'.
refuted.why: A +-1/2 dipole is a terminating lamina bundle (an edge dislocation of the stacking); there are 120 per section. A lamina that genuinely ends with k-1 and k+1 continuing, and another lamina beginning <= 2 mm further along at about the same z (the other member of the dipole's bundle, or a fragment), satisfies 'both neighbours link' and is BRIDGED: two different sheets become one id, and the BRIDGED status is then eligible for W7, which a fused ash face can pass. The rule as written is the nested-roll assumption that laminae only ever go missing, never end.
refuted.required_edit: Bridge only if all hold: (i) no +-1/2 defect of the per-section level-2 map within the gap plus one neighbourhood radius; (ii) the spacing between k-1 and k+1 across the gap stays ~2 x local pitch on both sides (neighbours closing up = lamina truly terminated -> TERMINATED; spacing growing = bundle inserted -> TERMINATED); (iii) the gap is not on a seam face or shear line (then it is a cut). Otherwise TERMINATED. W1 gains '0 bridges across injected dislocations/terminating bundles'.

refuted.item: Draft item 3: hairpin partner linking 'only if the ridge is continuous through the turn at level 2 (an explicit hairpin trace)'.
refuted.why: The operator is undefined: a ray along the layering normal (mostly z) cannot follow a turn whose apex is x-normal (38-46 % x-dominant normals in the edge columns, UMB-GEOMETRY-RESULT); a tangent-following 2-D trace is a different operator with no bars in the draft. Physically the inner layers of a fold of tens of sheets have turning radius below one sheet, are compressed (gaps closed, FUSED) or cracked, so only the outer layers of each fold are traceable; and at every -1/2 triradius (the point between two chevrons where the arms of fold A and fold B lie face to face) a ridge trace leaving A's apex can run onto B's arm, fusing two packets. The result's own reading ('alternating +1/2 and -1/2 down an edge column') says these triradii line the edge columns.
refuted.required_edit: Define the hairpin trace: in-section 2-D ridge following along the lamina tangent (anisotropic tensor, step <= 1 vox, no curvature bound) from the lamina's last OBSERVED point through the +1/2 to the first OBSERVED point of a lamina on the other arm; accepted only if the region enclosed by the trace and the z-ray between its endpoints contains exactly one +1/2, no -1/2 and no seam of the per-section map; the trace is itself a segment linked section-to-section along y; status HAIRPIN-OBSERVED. A trace passing within one neighbourhood radius of a -1/2 is cut. Inner laminae of a traced fold may be paired by nesting order only when the lamina counts between the traced lamina and the apex are equal on both arms, status INFERRED (no ink claim), else TERMINATED. W1 gains '0 partner links across a -1/2' and 'INFERRED pairing correct >= 98 % where equal counts hold'.

refuted.item: Draft item 4 X2: 'fused-core count: where the census says laminae are fused, sheets are counted by along-stacking density periodicity inside 1 mm slabs ... no winding number is claimed across a FUSED slab'.
refuted.why: 'Core' is the nested-roll leftover: UMB-PHERC0268-RESULT §1, §4 delivers no core. Fusion is distributed: the compression side of every fold interior, every PAIR/FUSED lamina, every ash-filled gap between seams. Autocorrelation periodicity assumes parallel, locally periodic laminae; inside a 1 mm window at a fold the normal tilts and the apparent pitch varies as 1/cos (to zero at the apex), and at level 0 the half-layer period (~35 um) and the fibre-bundle period (50-100 um, audit_spec X3) are competing periodicities that double or triple the count. A count from one pitch over a packet whose sheets vary 2:1 in thickness has an error of order the count itself.
refuted.required_edit: Rename 'fused-lamina count'; run on every PAIR/FUSED lamina of X1 (no core region), only on rays where the 16-section 3-D normal varies < 15 deg over the window and the ray-normal angle <= 15 deg; count = run thickness / local single-sheet pitch with the error propagated from the pitch p10-p90; no integer claimed when the error >= 1 sheet; periods < 0.8 w_s rejected (half-layer/fibre harmonics); confidence and the rejected-period record stored per slab. Fold interiors are counted only on the tension (open) side and reported as 'fused interior, count from the open side' otherwise.

refuted.item: Draft item 7 X5: 'per packet, a branch-local ordinal index from the packet's top/bottom envelope'.
refuted.why: A packet's envelope is a pair of seams, and seams every 1-4 mm are not conserved objects: the xz cuts (L3_xz_centre, L3_xz_leftedge) show seams branching and ending inside a section, the yz cut shows them terminating in swirls, and the result records that the folding changes along y. Where a seam closes, two packets merge and an envelope-counted ordinal jumps by the number of laminae of the merged packet without any lamina event; at every dipole the lamina count on a z-ray changes. The envelope ordinal therefore drifts silently along y and across x, which is exactly an index hop that W2 (per piece, modal class) will not see when it happens between pieces.
refuted.required_edit: Ordinal index counted from a tracked reference lamina of the packet (the lamina with the longest OBSERVED run), never from the envelope; a packet id is retired and new ids issued at every SEAM-OPEN / SEAM-CLOSE event (recorded in the event table); the offset between the old and new packets is KNOWN only where a reference lamina is OBSERVED through the event, else UNKNOWN.

refuted.item: Draft item 7 X5: 'a closure integer per tangent-tracked sheet (+1 expected)'.
refuted.why: +1 is the spiral-around-a-core invariant (audit_spec U5). UMB-PHERC0268-RESULT §1: the director index enclosed by 24 and 32 mm loops is 0 in three mid-scroll sections; these are not nested windings. A strip folded back and forth has index 0 (each +1/2 apex paired with a -1/2 triradius). 'Expected +1' would fail every correct trace, or reward a trace that hops across a fused fold interior, which is the one way to manufacture a closed loop in this geometry.
refuted.required_edit: Delete the closure-around-core integer. Replace with: (a) the Burgers count around each +-1/2 dipole (number of laminae terminating between its members, from the per-section map) as the cross-packet offset mechanism, generalising 'loop count around a terminating fault'; (b) a parity check: the recto/verso orientation of a traced sheet flips at every traced hairpin (checked against X3 where open); (c) 'absolute index' = number of traced (HAIRPIN-OBSERVED or INFERRED with equal counts) hairpins between the lamina and the top-envelope lamina along a path in the sheet graph, only for components in which every hairpin on the path is traced; the words 'winding number' are not used for PHerc0268.

refuted.item: Draft item 8 W10: 'normal gate against the fold-skeleton frame (withheld where the frame has no line within 10 mm)'.
refuted.why: A set of signed lines does not define a normal field, so the gate has no operand; the slit/affine model field it replaced (audit_spec W10) no longer exists for this scroll; gating the X1 rays against the in-section structure tensor would be circular (same operator).
refuted.required_edit: W10 = angle between the X4 mesh normal and the level-2 16-section 3-D structure-tensor normal (an operator the grower never saw) at each vertex: median <= 15 deg, p95 <= 30 deg; withheld where coherence < 0.5 or |n_y| > 0.5; no fold-skeleton term.

refuted.item: Draft item 8 W11 as adopted ('clean >= 90 % one-sheet, AMBIGUOUS <= 2 %; core reported') and draft item 5's 'grammar ... as in audit_spec.md X3' (R|R or V|V = fold if a hairpin is traced in adjacent tiles, else cleavage).
refuted.why: The 2 % bar was written for a nested roll with a ~14 % core. Here R|R / V|V contacts occur at every fold interior (120 folds per section, two or three bands plus both edge columns), and most apexes are fused or cracked so no in-plane hairpin is traced in adjacent tiles; the grammar's fallback 'else cleavage' then fuses the two arms of one fold, or two sheets facing R|R, into 'one cleaved sheet'. Absolute R/V names require a validated axis direction (audit_spec X3), and none exists (RESULT §1).
refuted.required_edit: R|R or V|V without a traced hairpin -> FOLD-UNTRACED (AMBIGUOUS) unless the thickness sum <= 1.2 w_s (true cleavage). W11 outcome fractions reported separately for flat-run tiles (the bar applies) and for fold-band / edge-column tiles (reported, no bar; a high AMBIGUOUS fraction there is the disclosed result). X3 outputs the alternation state only; no absolute R/V names for PHerc0268.

refuted.item: Draft item 9: 'X1 pilot on 128 sections centred on the longest fold-free band'.
refuted.why: No fold-free band exists: a defect is found in 86 of the 86 sections with a field, 120 per section, in two or three horizontal bands and both edge columns. A pilot chosen for fold-poverty exercises the flat-run path only and leaves the hairpin, dipole and PAIR/FUSED logic tested on the phantom alone, so the full pass would meet these for the first time with no real-data number behind it.
refuted.required_edit: Pilot = 128 level-2 sections at the y of median defect count, over the full xz section, with fragmentation statistics reported per region class (flat run / fold band / edge column, classes from the per-section defect density at 3 mm); the pilot must contain >= 20 hairpin-trace attempts and >= 50 dipoles and must report: fraction of laminae TERMINATED at folds, PAIR/FUSED fraction, HAIRPIN-OBSERVED success rate, bridges attempted vs refused by rule (i)-(iii). These numbers, with W8/W9, decide the full pass.

refuted.item: Draft item 8 W1: 'synthetic suite on a flattened concertina phantom (>= 192 sections, packets folded back and forth, ...)'.
refuted.why: The only existing flattened phantom (phantom.py --flat; pf2_xz_y200.png; UMB-PHANTOM-RESULT §2: 13 nested loops of a squashed spiral) is a nested roll, a geometry the measurement excludes (index +1 vs measured 0). The draft lists features but not that this is a new generator that must reproduce the measured defect statistics; a nested-spiral phantom with 'hairpins' tests a different partner rule (concentric U-turns with one +1/2 per edge) and would pass W1 while saying nothing about chevrons and triradii.
refuted.required_edit: W1 phantom = one inextensional strip folded back and forth: chevron bands at 2-3 z-levels plus edge columns of stacked apexes, generated section-wise to match the census: ~120 +-1/2 per section at R = 3 mm, mostly dipoles, fold-line persistence 11-35 mm with ~1 mm/mm obliqueness, seams every 1-4 mm, gaps closed (pitch = thickness) on the compression side of every fold and open on the tension side, sheet width = census w_s, debris, x-stripes, ash fill 0-100 %. Generator parameters and seeds hashed before any pilot record is read; the nested spiral phantom is recorded as not a W1 phantom. Bars added: 0 partner links across a -1/2; 0 bridges across injected dislocations; X2 count within +-1 on >= 90 % of fused fold interiors; INFERRED pairing correct >= 98 %; PAIR/FUSED classification correct on >= 98 % of contact runs.

refuted.item: Draft item 6 X4: 'sparse level-0 copy ... zeroed outside +-0.5 x local spacing of the X1 height map' and the far-side grow per patch.
refuted.why: In contact zones local spacing = sheet thickness, so +-0.5 x spacing is the sheet itself with no margin, while the X1 height uncertainty (re-anchor within 1.5 level-2 vox = 52 um, resampled to level 0) is about half a ~70-100 um sheet: the mask lands on the neighbour and the seed-mode grower hops inside a legal mask. At a fold apex the height map z_k(x, y) is undefined (two z per x), so there is no mask at all, and the grower is unmasked exactly where sheets are fused. The far-side grow (W6) then fails bimodally at every fold, which is correct, but the masked grow has already produced a surface across two sheets.
refuted.required_edit: Grow only ids of class SHEET whose clearance to both neighbours over the whole piece >= X1 height uncertainty + 0.5 w_s; mask half-width = max(0.5 x spacing, height uncertainty + 0.5 w_s), and where that exceeds the clearance the piece is not grown (status CONTACT, handed to X3). At HAIRPIN-OBSERVED turns the mask is the tube of the same half-width around the swept 2-D trace polyline; everywhere else the piece ends one spacing before the apex and the render mask carries TERMINATED there. INFERRED and CONTACT pieces are never rendered for ink.

refuted.item: Draft item 3: rays 'along the local layering normal (mostly z)' with only the per-section 2-D tensor (the audit_spec X1 '3-D tensor on 16-section sub-slabs for |n_z| and tilt' was dropped).
refuted.why: y-dominant normals reach 0.75 / 0.45 at the y ends and fold lines are oblique (~1 mm per 1.1 mm slab); a lamina tilted in y is crossed obliquely by an in-section ray, so its apparent width grows by 1/cos(tilt) (false PAIR/FUSED or false 'thickness change > 50 %' breaks) and its per-section z-displacement is systematic, not noise; the 8 end-face sections have no field at all.
refuted.required_edit: Restore the 16-section 3-D tensor; correct every width and spacing by cos of the y-tilt; exclude |n_y| > 0.5 as no-data; state the X1 y-domain explicitly as the rows where the 3-D field exists (the slanted end faces are outside it), so the 'full pass on 24 rows' is reported as the measured number of in-domain rows.

refuted.item: Draft item 3: 'm7 peaks secondary'.
refuted.why: audit_spec U9.10: m7 is blind in fused material (0.676 papyrus fraction for correct and jumped surfaces alike) and at level 1 is a binary th0.2 output; an m7 peak inside a raw-FUSED or PAIR run would create a lamina id through ash, i.e. a surface through two sheets, before W5 ever reports the disagreement.
refuted.required_edit: m7 peaks never create ids and never split a raw-FUSED, PAIR or HALF run; they only refine the position of an existing raw peak within +-1 vox; W5 compares raw-only and m7-only index maps as a finding, as written.

refuted.item: Draft item 8 W12 as a pass bar: 'reproducing >= 90 % of an organizer sheet's vertices within 0.25 x spacing' on PHerc0343P or PHerc0009B.
refuted.why: audit_spec W12 asks for reported hop/distance statistics, not a pass bar; organiser segments are not ground truth (their own hops) and those scrolls are nested rolls, so the run exercises only the flat-run path and says nothing about chevrons, triradii, dislocations or contact pairs.
refuted.required_edit: W12 reported as statistics (as in audit_spec), with the explicit note that it gives no evidence about the hairpin/dipole logic, which rests on W1 (phantom) and W14 (owner xz/yz audit) only.

missing: W13 (seam ZNCC in the unrolled strip) and W14 (owner cross-section audit in xz and yz, the retained final gate): the draft says 'W1-W12 unchanged' and item 9 applies the ink model 'after X4's bars', but audit_spec §4 says no ink model and no text claim before a piece passes W2, W3 AND W14; W14 is the only bar that looks at real cuts of a piece for hops across folds and must be named in item 8 and item 9.

The in-sheet slip measurement (audit_spec X1: sparse tangential 9 x 9 texture anchors every ~2 mm per segment matched every 8 sections) and the translational-fault / crossing-residue rules, with tears tested on the un-eroded crossing field; delaminated packets sliding along x is the main seam mechanism in a crushed stack and the draft has no measurement of it.

The ply-pair rule from audit_spec X5, re-stated thickness-based: 'two crossings closer than half the local spacing with no gap counted as one' would fuse every contact pair in a crushed stack; it must read 'two HALF runs whose thickness sum <= 1.2 w_s counted as one sheet'.
INFERRED as a status in the vocabulary (OBSERVED / BRIDGED / TERMINATED / INFERRED / CONTACT / HAIRPIN-OBSERVED), with the rule that INFERRED and CONTACT pieces carry no ink claim.

The per-section level-2 defect map as an X1 deliverable (sign, position, Burgers count, lifetime along y) and the census stratified by region class (flat run / fold band / edge column), with the separable fraction, pitch and w_s per class; the 0.3 launch gate marked (prov.) and applied per tile (tile-level no-data below it) rather than as one scroll-wide number.

An X2 phantom bar (count within +-1 on >= 90 % of fused slabs of known layer count, with half-layer and fibre periodicities injected) and the period-rejection record; X2 currently has no bar at all in item 8.
SEAM-OPEN / SEAM-CLOSE events in the event table, with packet ids retired and re-issued, and the offset KNOWN/UNKNOWN record across each event.

A coverage statement per piece and per 5 mm band (W4) that includes the fraction of piece boundary that is fold-terminated, and the expected dead zones: the edge columns at x = 14-17 mm and 84-92 mm, and every untraced fold interior, are outside the X1 domain unless hairpins are traced, so the rendered text will stop ~3-5 mm short of every fold; this consequence should be declared before the pilot.
The y-domain of X1 (rows where the 16-section 3-D field exists; |n_y| <= 0.5), so the '24 rows' and '7 lanes' are replaced by the measured in-domain count.

From audit_spec X3 gate 0: reading and recording the reconstruction's phase-retrieval parameter (delta/beta or filter length) before the existence test, since it sets the surviving texture scale; and the explicit statement that X3 produces alternation states only (no absolute R/V) for PHerc0268.

From audit_spec X1: the 1-D along-ray high-pass (no 3-D Gaussian) and the explicit 'nothing smoothed across sections beyond one step or across segments' clause; both are the anti-smooth-field guards and the draft dropped them.
keep: Item 0 entire: the R1/R2/R3 rejections with their failure modes, what survives of each, and the umbilicus transformed to a stacking-direction field plus fold frame with packet-wise tracing; no axis, no slit, no radial rays. Item 1: former roll axis along y, stacking along z over ~90 mm, ~120 defects per section mostly dipoles in two or three bands plus two edge columns, seams every 1-4 mm, level 3 resolves packets not windings, level 2 rows of 128 sections (1.44 GB, 24 rows) as the candidate working scale, level 1 only as bounded crops, level 0 never dense. Item 2: X0 as a measured census before any tracking, the timed level-2 row read, the m7 pooling method recorded, and 'if the census fails, the census is the result'. Item 3 core mechanics: per-section stripe removal (column z-median), oriented anisotropic tensor (<= 0.8 vox across, 3-4 along), raw-CT lamina/gap peaks primary with prominence >= 3 MAD, gated assignment with gate = 0.5 x locally measured spacing and prediction from the segment's own displacement, re-anchoring within min(1.5 vox, 0.3 x spacing), events never interpolated, cut after >= 3 lost points or coherence < 0.5, split and contact as two ids, break on thickness change > 50 % or displacement > 2 vox, the shear-line detector with every swept segment cut, independent +y/-y passes with disagreements flagged never averaged, TERMINATED as the default at a fold, the OBSERVED/BRIDGED/TERMINATED vocabulary, fragmentation statistics from a 128-section pilot before any full run. Item 5: the X3 existence test (power spectrum against a phase-randomised null) gating the whole stage, ink downstream of geometry. Item 6: VC3D seed-mode grower unchanged, one unmasked far-side grow per patch, arc-length parametrisation along the tracked polyline, render masks carrying status, pieces.py as the trust unit. Item 7: cross-packet offsets only by a traced hairpin or a loop count, else UNKNOWN; absolute numbers only for a component with every offset known and every cycle closed; everything else (packet id, local index); the orchestrator claims no letters. Item 8: the W2-W9 numbers as written, 'any failed bar stops the stage; nothing is lowered; a failed pilot is the deliverable of that stage'. Item 9: the order census -> pilot -> phantom and W8/W9 -> full pass -> renders -> ink last with the FL-7 bars unchanged.

refuted.item: Sections 1 and 9: "streamed in y-rows of 128 sections (1.44 GB each, 24 rows) split across the lane containers" and "the full X1 pass on 7 lanes (3-4 y-rows each)" as the whole resident budget for X1.
refuted.why: 1.44 GB (128 x 3709 x 3037 uint8) is the CT row only. Section 3 reads m7 as the secondary channel, so each row also carries an m7 row: 1.44 GB if level-2 m7 is 128^3-chunked, but audit_spec.md records m7 as 192^3 zstd chunks at level 3 and its level-2 .zarray as unverified; a 192-section m7 chunk column is 192 x 3709 x 3037 = 2.16 GB, and 8 of the 24 CT rows (lcm(128,192) = 384: rows 1, 4, 7, ...) straddle two m7 columns. The only existing y-row reader (S3Blocks in tools/umb/st_axis.py) holds the old and the new row during a row change (CT peak 2.88 GB) and, for a straddling slice, keeps both columns alive while it concatenates them (m7 peak 2 x 2.16 + 1.44 = 5.8 GB). Its slab pattern `stack.astype(np.float32)` applied to a 128-section row is 5.8 GB. audit_spec X1 adds a cached adjacent row for the 3-D sub-slab tensor halo (+2.9-3.6 GB); the draft dropped that tensor but not the halo, and audit_spec U8/section 3 keep a 4.8 GB level-3/4 /dev/shm cache per container life (tmpfs is RAM). Worst case 2.9 + 5.8 + 1.8 (four per-section float32 workers) + 4.8 + ~1 = 16 GB on a 15 GB container, violating the recorded rule of no launch below 8 GB available. The draft states none of these bytes, so the lane split cannot be shown to run.
refuted.required_edit: Replace with: "y-rows of 128 sections: 1.44 GB CT (128 x 3709 x 3037 uint8, 696 chunks of 2 MB; a single xz section is spread over all 696, so the row is the minimum read) plus the m7 row (1.44 GB if 128^3 chunks; if 192^3, read per m7 chunk column and sliced to the row before the next column is fetched, peak 2.16 + 1.44 GB; never two columns concatenated). One row resident per channel; the reader releases the old row before fetching the next (transient +1.44 GB CT). All processing per section or per <= 16-section sub-slab in float32 (<= 0.72 GB); a float32 row (5.8 GB) and any 3-D 1 mm Gaussian (10-14 GB per row) are never materialised. No adjacent row is cached: the draft has no 3-D sub-slab tensor and linking needs only the previous section's ridge table. X1 lanes carry no level-3/4 /dev/shm cache (the W9 lane alone keeps the 2.4 GB level 3). Declared ceiling RSS + tmpfs <= 11 GB; `free -m` >= 8 GB available logged before every row. 7 lanes x 3-4 rows = 4.3-5.8 GB CT + the same for m7 per lane, 12-16 min of fetch per sweep at 12 MB/s."

refuted.item: Section 3 "independent +y and -y passes" combined with section 9's lane split, with no lane schedule and no boundary stitch.
refuted.why: A streamed row supports only the sweep whose predecessor state exists; the -y sweep over a lane's rows needs the state of the following row, so it is a second sweep over the data. Either every row is fetched twice (68 GB CT + m7 instead of 34 GB; +12-16 min per lane, feasible but unstated) or the per-section ridge tables are cached: upper bound 3037 rays x ~372 peaks (90 mm / 7 vox) x 8 B = 9 MB per section, 1.16 GB per row, 4.6 GB per 4-row lane, which exceeds the 1 GB disk and fits tmpfs only inside the ceiling of item 1. The draft states neither. The 6 lane boundaries carry no tracker state, so every segment is cut there, i.e. every 384-512 sections = 13-18 mm along y, shorter than the measured 20-35 mm fold-axis coherence (UMB-PHERC0268-RESULT 3); the fragmentation statistics, W8 and W9 would be capped by the lane split, not by the scroll.
refuted.required_edit: Add to section 9: "Per lane: phase A fetches each row once and writes the per-section ridge table (record layout and ray stride declared; <= 0.5 GB per row in tmpfs, else rows are fetched twice and the bytes are counted); phase B runs the +y and -y sweeps on the tables, one core each (2 x 128 x 4-8 s = 17-34 min per row per direction; ~2-3 h per 4-row lane in all). Each lane exports the ridge tables and segment states of its two boundary sections; a stitch step links segments across the 6 lane boundaries with the same gated assignment (gate 0.5 x local spacing, same event rules) and records every stitch in the event table; a lane-boundary cut is never a TERMINATED event."

refuted.item: Section 3 Outputs: "per-branch height maps z_k(x, y) with status OBSERVED / BRIDGED / TERMINATED" (full resolution implied; no dtype, no decimation, no store).
refuted.why: A full-resolution int16 map per branch over the section extent is 3037 x 3037 x 2 B = 18.4 MB; with ~372 sheet crossings across the 90 mm stack at the >= 7-vox (0.24 mm) domain spacing the upper bound is ~6.9 GB. The lane disk is 1.1 GB and holds JSON/PNG only, tmpfs is RAM, and audit_spec X0 states that large arrays have no home and deliverables are decimated. audit_spec X1 specifies int16 maps on decimated tifxyz grids (10-vox cells: ~0.18 MB per full-extent branch, < 70 MB in all) plus a full-resolution sparse event table; the draft dropped both qualifiers.
refuted.required_edit: Replace with: "Outputs: per-branch int16 height maps on 10-vox tifxyz grids with status OBSERVED / BRIDGED / TERMINATED (bytes per lane recorded; total < 1 GB; committed to the repo as the durable store), the full-resolution sparse event table, and full-resolution per-piece maps (<= 1 MB per 2 x 2 cm piece at level 2) generated only for pieces entering X4."

refuted.item: Section 9: "X1 pilot on 128 sections centred on the longest fold-free band (one lane, ~2 h)".
refuted.why: No fold-free y-band exists in the measured geometry: 86 of 95 level-3 sections carry ~120 defects each (14,176 in all; the one defect-free section is a single section), the fold-rich bands are horizontal bands inside each xz section, and the fold axes are y-segments of 20-35 mm at both x-edge columns and in the interior (UMB-PHERC0268-RESULT 2-3). A window centred on a band is not chunk-aligned, so 128 sections cost two CT rows (2.9 GB) plus two m7 columns, and the ~2 h holds only for one row: fetch 1.44 + <= 2.2 GB (3-5 min), per-section preprocessing (~1.4e9 trilinear samples, minutes on 4 cores), tracker 2 x 128 x 4-8 s = 17-34 min, W8 on the same row.
refuted.required_edit: Replace with: "X1 pilot on one chunk-aligned level-2 row [128k, 128k+128) (= 4 level-3 slabs), k chosen outside the no-field end-face slabs (level-3 y < 240, i.e. level-2 rows 0-3, and the last no-field slab) as the row whose 4 slabs have the lowest defect count in logs/umb/PHerc0268/defects.json; the pilot domain inside the row is whatever passes the X1 domain gate; one lane, ~2 h (fetch 3-5 min, preprocessing minutes, tracker 17-34 min per direction, W8 on the resident row)."

refuted.item: Section 8 W12: "an external reference-only run on a scroll with organizer segments (PHerc0343P or PHerc0009B) reproducing >= 90 % of an organizer sheet's vertices within 0.25 x spacing", placed by section 9 on the pilot before any full pass.
refuted.why: Neither scroll is in the data plan: audit_spec section 3 lists the usable controls as PHerc1451, 0800, 1447, 0841, 0139 at levels 3-4 and the licence-gated Paris 4; 0343P and 0009B appear only in the 2.4 um <-> 8.64 um transform listing for the deferred ink gate. audit_spec W12 reports absolute hop/distance statistics with no pass threshold, so the >= 90 % / 0.25 x spacing bar has no basis in the files. The run is a second scroll's rows through the proxy (>= 1.4 GB per row at the 8.64 um protocol; for a 2.4 um volume the level with 34.56 um voxels and its bytes are unknown) plus its organiser segments, with no fetch, RAM or lane budget, inside a schedule that gives the pilot lane ~2 h.
refuted.required_edit: Replace with: "W12: X1 on one chunk-aligned row of a scroll named from audit_spec section 3 that has an audited organiser segmentation not used for anything else; its volume id, level, voxel size, row bytes and timed fetch are recorded before the run; report absolute hop/distance statistics against the organiser sheet (the spec's wording); any pass threshold is declared (prov.) with its basis before the run; it runs on its own lane and its fetch and tracker time are added to section 9."

refuted.item: Section 2: "If the separable fraction of the mask is < 0.3 the tracker is not launched".
refuted.why: audit_spec X0 asks for the separability fraction per y-row and sets no threshold; no measured value in UMB-PHERC0268-RESULT or UMB-GEOMETRY-RESULT supports 0.3; the spec's rule is that a provisional threshold is marked (prov.) and fixed from the phantom and the clean-zone distribution before it is quoted as a bar.
refuted.required_edit: Write "< 0.3 (prov.; fixed from the W1 phantom's separable fraction at the measured spacing and declared before the census is read)" and report the fraction per y-row, not only for the mask as a whole.

missing: X0 (section 2) omits the three records audit_spec X0 requires that fix the X1 budget: the m7 level-2 .zarray (shape, chunks, compressor, dtype) and level-3 histogram; a timed m7 row or chunk column through the proxy next to the timed CT row (1.44 GB: 120 s at 12 MB/s dense, ~70 s if only in-mask chunks are stored as at level 3, 56 %), with `free -m` before and after; and the named durable store (JSON/tifxyz to the repo; the 1 GB lane disk holds nothing else). Also the census cost itself: 20 sections spread over y are up to 20 distinct rows = up to 29 GB of row reads (40 min at 12 MB/s dense, ~22 min at the 56 % in-mask fraction), one row resident at a time; this is what makes "one lane, ~1 h" true and it should be written down.

X2, X3 and X5 are absent from the order and compute of section 9. X3 gate 0: >= 20 level-0 256^3 tiles (16.8 MB CT each, chunk-aligned 128^3) plus m7, < 0.5 GB and minutes, axis-free, so it may run in parallel on a clean outer slab (audit_spec section 4). Full X3 only if gate 0 opens: 7k-21k tiles = 118-353 GB of level-0 CT at 12 MB/s (2.7-8.2 h aggregate fetch) and 39-117 h of tile compute at ~20 s per tile (6-17 h per lane on 7 lanes), RSS + tmpfs <= 12 GB with the <= 2 GB chunk LRU (audit_spec X7). X2: ~0.6 GB per 1 mm ROI at level 0 (75 MB at level 1), with the ROI count declared by the census.

X4 has no patch budget. Per 2 x 2 cm patch: 1.6-2 GB of level-0 m7 chunks (2.3-2.8 min at 12 MB/s), 100-300 MB sparse zarr, VC3D cache_root and render, all in /dev/shm because the 1 GB disk cannot hold them; two 21-min grows (1275 s measured on i98) and < 10 min of metrics: ~1 h per patch per lane, ~170 patches per day on 7 lanes. The scroll's sheet area (~187 windings x ~170 mm perimeter x 105 mm ~ 3.3 m^2) is ~8,000 patches, ~50 lane-days, so section 9 needs a declared piece-selection rule and patch count, and X1 rows must be released from RAM before X4 runs on the same lane.

Pilot-lane RAM for the bars: W9's chained level-3 block matches need the 2.4 GB level-3 cache in /dev/shm on the pilot lane (1.44 CT + <= 2.2 m7 + 2.4 + transients ~ 8 GB); state it. W1/W9 phantom scale and footprint: level-2 voxels (34.56 um; sheets 3-6 vox, 1.5-vox sheets as the stress case), generated section-wise at the U7 extent (2400 x 2800 level-2 px = 6.7 MB per section; 192 sections = 1.3 GB, the W9 >= 512-section phantom = 3.4 GB, tmpfs only), regenerated from the seed for the -y sweep rather than held.

Aggregate proxy throughput with 7 lanes fetching at once: the ~12 MB/s is per container with 32 threads and is "to be re-measured per container"; whether it is shared across lanes is unmeasured. If shared, the full-pass fetch is 7x longer (still ~1-2.5 h aggregate for 34-68 GB CT + m7); measure once with all lanes active and record it in V13/W4 run records.

Rows with no layering field (level-3 end-face slabs y < 240 = level-2 rows 0-3, and the far-end no-field slabs: 8 of 95 sections in UMB-PHERC0268-RESULT) should be excluded from the lane split or counted at zero coverage in W4; the 3-4 rows per lane should be assigned after this exclusion.

The 1-D along-ray high-pass and the explicit prohibition of a 3-D 1 mm Gaussian (10-14 GB per row) from audit_spec X1, dropped by the draft; and the ridge-table record layout and ray stride (declared before the pilot, since they bound the tmpfs use of the two-sweep schedule).
The ink stage's input: section 9 says the FL-7 model is applied to rendered pieces after X4's bars; the render bytes per piece and where they live (tmpfs, then decimated to the repo) are not stated.
keep: The byte arithmetic of section 1 is right and should stay: level 2 = 3709 x 3037 x 3037 uint8 = 34.2 GB; a chunk-aligned y-row of 128 sections = 1.44 GB (696 chunks of 2 MB); 24 rows (3037/128 = 23.7); sheet 100-200 um = 1.5-3 vox at level 3 and 3-6 vox at level 2; level 1 (17.28 um) only as bounded crops; level 0 never densely. Level 2 as the working scale and the y-row as the read unit are justified (one xz section is spread over all 696 chunks of its row, so the row is the minimum read; S3Blocks axis=1 in tools/umb/st_axis.py already implements it and keeps one row, and the level-3 y-run measured 95 slabs over 12 chunk-rows in 1321 s). Keep X0 as a census-first gate that can end the stage, and its ~1 h on one lane (feasible: <= 20 rows, ~29 GB, 22-40 min of fetch). Keep the pilot-before-full-pass order and ~2 h for one chunk-aligned row (fetch 3-5 min, tracker 17-34 min per direction). Keep the per-section X1 operator set (column z-median stripe removal, oriented anisotropic tensor, raw-CT ray peaks primary with m7 secondary, gated assignment at 0.5 x measured spacing, re-anchoring, the event rules, shear-line cuts, hairpin termination unless traced), the domain gate, and 'a failed pilot is the deliverable'. Keep X2 as a deferred separately gated count, X3 gate 0 as a cheap axis-free existence test, X4's reliance on the spec's measured per-patch numbers (1.6-2 GB of m7 chunks, 1275 s per grow, two grows), X5's (packet id, local index) rule with absolute winding numbers only for fully closed adjacency components, and the cost-based rejections (dense flow 137 GB at level 2 is one float32 per voxel, a 3-vector would be 410 GB, so the rejection stands a fortiori; nnUNet 100-200 CPU-days). Keep the bars W1-W11 by reference to audit_spec with the fold-skeleton adaptation of W10.

refuted.item: Section 8 preamble: "Bars (W1-W12 of audit_spec.md, unchanged, with the geometry-specific additions)"
refuted.why: audit_spec.md X6 has W1-W14. The draft silently drops W13 (seam ZNCC in the unrolled strip, median >= 0.5, no seam offset > 2 px) and W14 (owner cross-section audit in xz and yz, 'retained final gate until W2-W7 reproduce the owner's verdict on the nine ring1 patches'), and alters W2, W3, W5, W6, W7, W9, W10 and W12. W13 is the only seam-consistency bar and W14 the only gate independent of the pipeline's own outputs; the draft keeps 'pieces.py stays the trust unit' while removing the audit that defines trust. Section 9 likewise loses the spec's section-4 rule 'no ink model and no text claim before a piece passes W2, W3 and W14, and never across a BRIDGED or UNVERIFIED crack'.
refuted.required_edit: Replace with: "Bars W1-W14 of audit_spec.md X6, with the changes listed here and no others:" and restore W13 and W14 verbatim. In section 9 replace "the ink model (DECL-FL-7) is applied to rendered pieces only after X4's bars" with "no ink model and no text claim before a piece passes W2 (unmasked), W3, W13 and W14, and never across a BRIDGED, UNVERIFIED or HAIRPIN-UNVERIFIED vertex".

refuted.item: W2: "index continuity along the mesh >= 98 % of vertices in the modal class per piece, 0 index steps inside a piece"
refuted.why: Circular as written. X4 grows the mesh inside a surface volume zeroed outside +-0.5 x local spacing of the X1 height map, so an index read from the X1 map along that mesh is continuous by construction; the bar validates X1 with X1. The spec's W2 reads the index from 'raw-CT rays along the layering normal' and adds 'FUSED fraction < 10 % or the piece is split' and the retrospective on ring1 i98/i96/i99/i101/i103 re-cut in xz and yz (xsec cuts z only today) that 'must reproduce the owner's marks or the detector is not used'; all three are dropped. '0 index steps' is also reachable by a wrong pipeline if vertices with no index (no data / FUSED) are ignored.
refuted.required_edit: W2: "index at each mesh vertex recomputed from raw-CT rays along the local layering normal, independent of the X1 height map and of the mask; computed on the masked grow AND on the unmasked far-side grow; >= 98 % of vertices in the modal class per piece, 0 index steps inside a piece, fraction of vertices with no index reported and any piece whose mesh crosses a no-data/FUSED cell is split there; FUSED fraction < 10 % or the piece is split; retrospective: the detector re-run on ring1 i98/i96/i99/i101/i103 after re-cutting them in xz and yz (xsec extended first) must reproduce the owner's marks or the detector is not used."

refuted.item: W3: "neighbour clearance >= 0.5 x local spacing for >= 98 % of vertices"
refuted.why: 'Local spacing' is X1's own estimate; a tracker that merged two laminae into one FUSED lamina overestimates spacing and passes. On the masked grow the mesh cannot leave the +-0.5-spacing band, so clearance >= 0.5 spacing is near-guaranteed by construction. The spec's 'FUSED counts as fail; < 0.3 masked from the render' is dropped.
refuted.required_edit: W3: "clearance = distance along the local normal from each vertex to the nearest raw-CT lamina peak on either side (prominence >= 3 MAD), measured on the raw profile, not from the X1 spacing map, on both the masked and the unmasked grow; >= 0.5 x the locally measured spacing for >= 98 % of vertices; a FUSED profile (width > 8 vox) counts as fail; vertices < 0.3 x spacing are masked from the render and their fraction reported."

refuted.item: W5: "raw-only vs m7-only agreement reported"
refuted.why: Drops the spec's 'm7 seam-bridging test; disagreement is a finding about m7'. The measured geometry has large horizontal seams every 1-4 mm, and m7 is the surface volume both X4 grows read; if m7 bridges a seam, the masked and unmasked grows cross it in agreement and W6 cannot detect it. Without the seam test there is no bar that tells whether m7 may be used as the grower volume at all.
refuted.required_edit: W5: "raw-only vs m7-only index agreement per ray, reported per y-row; m7 seam-bridging test: on every detected seam in the pilot rows, the fraction of crossings where m7 is continuous while the raw profile shows air on both sides; disagreement is a finding about m7; a (prov.) ceiling declared before the pilot above which m7 is demoted to comparator-only for that row and X4 is not run there."

refuted.item: W6: "masked vs unmasked grow >= 95 % within 0.25 x spacing"
refuted.why: Drops the spec's 'bimodal separation fails the crack'. A pooled 95 % over a patch hides a one-sheet jump of the unmasked grow at a seam near the patch edge (fewer than 5 % of vertices are beyond it), which is precisely the event the bar exists to catch.
refuted.required_edit: W6: ">= 95 % of overlapping vertices within 0.25 x spacing AND, per detected crack/seam crossed by the patch, no contiguous region of overlapping vertices separated by more than 0.25 x spacing (bimodal separation fails that crack and relabels it UNVERIFIED); reported per crack and per piece, never pooled only."

refuted.item: W7: "fibre-bundle continuity across BRIDGED cracks >= 80 % above the one-spacing null"
refuted.why: (a) Not computable at the draft's working scale: the spec records fibres as 'resolution at 8.64 um marginal, absent at 34.6/69 um', and the draft allows level 1 only as bounded crops and level 0 'never densely' without saying W7 reads level 0 at each crack; no crop count or budget. (b) The phrase is ambiguous and drops the spec's definition (2-D template, lags to +-0.5 mm, equal tensor direction within 10 deg, above the p95 of the one-spacing null) and its action (failures relabelled UNVERIFIED). (c) Scope: only BRIDGED cracks are tested, so a tracker that carries a sheet through a debris- or ash-filled seam as OBSERVED is never tested by the one bar that uses data the tracker did not see.
refuted.required_edit: W7: "at every BRIDGED crack and at a declared random sample (>= 20 % and >= 30) of OBSERVED segments crossing a detected seam, read a level-0 chunk-aligned tile on each side; 2-D template of the fibre-bundle texture (period 50-100 um), lags to +-0.5 mm, tensor direction equal within 10 deg; the crossing passes if its correlation exceeds the p95 of the one-spacing null (template matched one spacing above and below); >= 80 % of BRIDGED cracks pass or the stage fails; every failing crossing, bridged or observed, is relabelled UNVERIFIED; tile count and read volume recorded in X0's budget."

refuted.item: W8: "forward/backward and +y/-y agreement median <= 0.5 vox, p95 <= 1.5 vox" (and its use as a pilot gate in section 9)
refuted.why: Self-agreement of one detector run twice. The draft's own X1 text says integer-spacing slip has |d| ~ 0 and perfect correlation, so two-direction checks cannot see it; the spec marks W8 'necessary only: no hop-detection claim'. The draft lists it as a bar without the qualifier and makes it one of three pilot gates, so a tracker that jumps sheets consistently in both directions passes the pilot.
refuted.required_edit: Append to W8: "necessary only; agreement is not evidence of sheet identity and no hop-detection claim follows from it." Remove W8 from the pilot's pass criteria in section 9 (keep it reported).

refuted.item: W9: "drift <= 2 vox at level 2 for 95 % of chained blocks"
refuted.why: Drops the spec's loop closure (the only reference-free consistency check) and the >= 512-section real-slab phantom with real debris, stripes and an integer-spacing shear. The reference, chained level-3 block matches, is the estimator the spec rejected as a prior because 'periodic blocks fail the ratio test and the prior becomes a debris-motion field'; drift against it is drift relative to debris. Chain length is unstated, and a level-3 block match has at best ~1 level-3 voxel = 2 level-2 voxel precision, i.e. the bar's own size, unless sub-voxel fitting is declared.
refuted.required_edit: W9: "tracker displacement integrated over a declared chain length (sections) vs chained level-3 block matches at 16-section steps, blocks failing the ratio test excluded and the excluded fraction reported, loop-closure residual reported; reference precision (sub-voxel fit method) stated and shown < 1/3 of the bar on the phantom; <= 2 vox at level 2 for 95 % of blocks; plus the >= 512-section real-slab phantom with real debris, stripes and an integer-spacing shear; necessary only."

refuted.item: W10: "normal gate against the fold-skeleton frame (withheld where the frame has no line within 10 mm)"
refuted.why: Undefined: the fold skeleton is 20 stable defect lines with signs and extents (UMB-PHERC0268-RESULT item 3); it defines no normal field to gate against. The only measured normal field is the stacking-direction field (3-D structure tensor, |n_z| median 0.76), and mesh-normal vs structure-tensor of the same CT is blind to a sheet jump (a jumped surface has the same normal). The withholding rule would withhold the gate over most of the volume: the lines are 11-35 mm long on a 105 mm scroll and none spans it.
refuted.required_edit: W10: "mesh normal vs the level-3 stacking-direction field (3-D structure tensor on 16-section sub-slabs, coherence >= 0.5): median <= 15 deg, p95 reported; withheld where field coherence < 0.5; necessary only, blind to identity. The fold skeleton marks hairpin zones for X1 and X5 and is not a normal reference."

refuted.item: W12: "an external reference-only run on a scroll with organizer segments (PHerc0343P or PHerc0009B) reproducing >= 90 % of an organizer sheet's vertices within 0.25 x spacing"
refuted.why: (a) Neither scroll is in the spec's same-protocol control list (1451, 0800, 1447, 0841, 0139); the spec requires a bucket listing before anything is scheduled on them; RULES.md:308 records no m7 on their 8.64 um volumes, so X1's secondary channel and the X4 grower have no surface volume there. (b) 'Never used for anything else' fails on both: 0343P is benchmark-only (RULES.md:45) and the DECL-FL-7 held-out scroll (RULES.md:5662); 0009B segments are KTLB-M training labels (RULES.md:243). (c) The >= 90 % within 0.25 x spacing pass bar is invented; the spec says 'report absolute hop/distance statistics'. An organiser segmentation is another pipeline's output, so agreement with it is not correctness and reproducing it is reachable by a pipeline that shares its errors. (d) No U0 frame test or X0 census is required on the external scroll. (e) Section 9 schedules W12 'on the pilot', which is on 0268.
refuted.required_edit: W12: "external reference-only run: X1 (raw-only where no m7 exists) on one same-protocol scroll with an 8.64 um volume and an audited organiser segmentation that has been used for nothing else in this project, chosen after a recorded bucket listing and its own U0 frame test and X0 census; report absolute hop and distance statistics against the organiser sheet (median, p95, fraction within 0.25 x spacing); no pass threshold is declared; the result is a finding, not a gate." Remove W12 from section 9's pilot gates and schedule it as its own step.

refuted.item: Section 1 (headed '(measured)'): "level 3 resolves packets, not single windings (sheet 100-200 um = 1.5-3 voxels, gaps mostly unresolved). Therefore the working scale is level 2 (34.56 um; sheet 3-6 voxels)"
refuted.why: No sheet thickness has been measured on PHerc0268 in any of the four files; audit_spec.md X0 says the pitch/thickness/gap histogram is the census's job and the assumed values are unsupported. 100-200 um is the phantom generator's thickness parameter (audit_kept.json: 'thickness 100-200 um'; UMB-PHANTOM-RESULT item 2: 0.15 mm sheets), i.e. a phantom setting has leaked into the 'measured geometry' section. The one measured number is ~35 um per half-layer from one probed m7 chunk (spec X3), i.e. ~70 um per sheet = 2 level-2 voxels, which would put X1's domain (spacing >= 7 vox with a visible gap) in doubt. The level-2 choice is a consequence of an unmeasured premise.
refuted.required_edit: Strike the parenthesis and 'Therefore'. Write: "sheet thickness, pitch and gap width are unmeasured on 0268 until the X0 census (one probed m7 chunk gives ~35 um per half-layer); level 2 is the provisional working scale and is confirmed only if the census's separable fraction clears the declared (prov.) 0.3; otherwise the census is the result."

refuted.item: Section 1: "coherent fold axes 20-35 mm long along y"
refuted.why: UMB-PHERC0268-RESULT item 3 measured 1,656 tracked lines, 90 persisting >= 10 sections (>= 11 mm), 20 passing the stability bar, longest run 32-35 mm. '20-35 mm' is not the measured distribution.
refuted.required_edit: Replace with: "20 stable fold lines, each persisting >= 11 mm along y, the longest 32-35 mm; none spans the 105 mm length."

refuted.item: Section 3 X1 hairpin clause: "linked to its partner on the other side of the hairpin only if the ridge is continuous through the turn at level 2 (an explicit hairpin trace), else TERMINATED"
refuted.why: audit_spec.md X1 marks hairpin zones 'no data'. The draft adds a new identity operation with no operator (the along-normal rays and the ray-normal <= 30 deg domain rule both fail at |n_x| > 0.7, by the draft's own text) and no real-data validation: the only bar is W1's phantom count. X5 then makes the traced hairpin the sole source of cross-packet offsets, so an unverified link propagates directly into absolute winding numbers. Fold radii of 0.3-3 mm (U7) are 9-87 level-2 voxels, so the inner side of a tight turn is one or two voxels of lamina.
refuted.required_edit: Define the operator (2-D ridge following in the section along the tangent direction, independent of the along-normal rays) and the acceptance (raw-CT and m7 ridge both continuous through the turn over >= N consecutive sections, N declared). Every real-data hairpin link carries status HAIRPIN-UNVERIFIED until a level-1 crop of that turn is recorded and reviewed under W14; X5 uses only verified hairpins for offsets; the number of links in each state is reported per packet.

refuted.item: Section 7 X5: "a closure integer per tangent-tracked sheet (+1 expected)"
refuted.why: Carried over from the slit frame. UMB-PHERC0268-RESULT item 1 measured director index 0 inside loops of radius 24-32 mm in three mid-scroll sections: these are not nested windings around a core. A loop at fixed local index that does not pass through traced hairpins at both x extremes closes with 0, and one that does requires hairpin links at both edge columns, where the tracker's domain rule gives no data. '+1 expected' is a claim, not a measurement, in this geometry.
refuted.required_edit: Replace with: "a closure integer only for a loop at fixed local index that closes through verified hairpins at both x extremes; otherwise no closure is reported and the sheet carries (packet id, local index) only; no expected value is declared."

refuted.item: Section 9: "X0 census (one lane, ~1 h); X1 pilot on 128 sections centred on the longest fold-free band (one lane, ~2 h)"
refuted.why: audit_spec.md X7 says the identity pass is 'I/O-bound and unscheduled until one row is timed'; the ~1 h and ~2 h are estimates presented beside measured numbers. 'The longest fold-free band' along y is not measured anywhere: the RESULT gives fold-rich bands in x and fold-line segments 11-35 mm long distributed along y, not a fold-free y-range; choosing the easiest band after the fact biases the pilot's fragmentation statistics, which are the pilot's deliverable.
refuted.required_edit: Mark both times '(est.; replaced by the X0 timed row read)'. Pilot placement by a declared rule recorded before any tracker output is seen: one 128-section row at the median per-section defect count and one at the p90 (fold-rich); both pilots' fragmentation statistics reported.

refuted.item: Section 9 pilot gates: "bars W1 (phantom, local) and W8/W9/W12 on the pilot before any full pass"
refuted.why: audit_spec.md section 4 item 5 gates the pilot on W1, the W2 retrospective, W4 and W5. The draft replaces them with W8 (self-agreement), W9 (block-match drift) and W12 (another scroll, not 'on the pilot'); a tracker that jumps sheets consistently passes W8 and W9, and the draft's set contains no bar that uses data the tracker did not see.
refuted.required_edit: Replace with: "pilot gates: W1 with freeze hash recorded, W2 on the unmasked grow plus the ring1 retrospective, W4, W5 including the m7 seam test, the W7 sample; W8 and W9 reported as necessary-only; W12 scheduled separately."

refuted.item: Section 8 W1 phantom bars as a validation of the real pipeline (no freeze, no level, undefined injection)
refuted.why: audit_spec.md U7 requires generator parameters and seeds hashed (METRIC-HASH) before any run record is read, and audit_kept.json records that this rule was already violated once (the flattened sweep is post-hoc). A phantom built with the tracker's own assumptions (1.5-vox sheets, pitch, fold radius) and iterated against the tracker is reachable by a wrong pipeline. The phantom's level and section size are unstated (U7's are level-3 sizes; X1 runs at level 2), V0 on the phantom is not required, and 'injected one-sheet jumps flagged on 100 %' names no injection geometry, although the spec puts injected jumps among perturbations of real 0268 data.
refuted.required_edit: W1: add "generator parameters and seeds hashed before the pilot's first section is read; hash quoted in the declaration; phantom generated at level-2 geometry (section size stated) and passing V0; injected one-sheet jump = a one-local-spacing z-shift of a region bounded by a line at a declared angle, applied to real level-2 sections from a declared y in >= 20 placements including integer-spacing cases; flagged = shear line detected within +-2 sections of the injection and every swept segment cut. Phantom passes are evidence about code paths only, never about 0268."

refuted.item: Section 6 X4 as written (no self-intersection/crossing test)
refuted.why: audit_spec.md X4 requires 'an external mesh self-intersection/crossing test (the grower has none)'; the draft keeps the grower and the trust unit but drops the only topological check on the mesh.
